question: Does a so-called Ming-print label establish a physical Ming printing, the author's original 1619 article text, or the 1827/1869 repaired leaf?
scholar_abstract_claims: Historical claims of a Ming printed edition are contested; author argues the reported proofs do not establish an actual Ming printed edition.
The purported Ming-printed exemplar recorded by Li Ciming is interpreted by author as Zhou Xingyi's old manuscript now in Taiwan.
Scholar assigns high textual importance to the old manuscript as potentially retaining the 1619 authorial configuration.

old manuscript with a physically proven Ming printed edition
